stories.title: SC grants post-arrest bail to 4 suspects in human placenta smuggling case
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) on Monday granted post-arrest bail to four suspects arrested in a case relating to the alleged illegal purchase and sale of human placentas.

Deputy Attorney General Raja Shafqat Abbasi told Dawn that, acting on credible information about the illegal collection, processing, storage and commercial trade of human placentas, a joint team of the FIA’s CCC and HOTA raided a house in Islamabad’s Sector F-7/1.

According to the preliminary investigation, the suspects were allegedly acting in connivance with one another and were involved in the illegal collection, preservation, storage, processing, packaging and export of human placentas for commercial gain.

stories.title: At ECO meeting, Araghchi calls for reliable, sustainable regional energy mechanism
summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed the need for a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism on Monday, as he addressed the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers in Islamabad.

Dar said Pakistan desired a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan, but meaningful progress towards regional cooperation required the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism.
The meeting was attended by senior officials from ECO member states, representatives of the ECO Secretariat, and delegates from the organisation’s specialised agencies and regional institutions.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl's murder case: Islamabad court grants police 4-day physical remand suspects
summary: The suspects were presented before Judicial Magistrate Naima Iffat at the district and sessions court in Islamabad by police, who sought their eight-day physical remand.
However, the court approved four-day physical remand of the suspects after initially reserving its decision on the police request.

The suspects were arrested on Sunday after a first information report (FIR) was registered under Section 302 (intentional murder) of the Pakistan Penal Code at the Shams Colony police station on the complaint of the 13-year-old girl’s father.

stories.title: Lawyers submit affidavits detailing Nov 11 meeting with Imran, Bushra at Adiala jail
summary: ISLAMABAD: Lawyers representing former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, have submitted affidavits to the Islamabad High Court (IHC), detailing their Nov 11 meeting with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail.

According to the affidavits, the meeting was arranged pursuant to an order passed by the IHC on November 10, directing the jail authorities to facilitate a meeting between Imran, Bushra and their lawyers at Adiala jail.
According to the application, medical records furnished by the Adiala jail superintendent had revealed that Bushra’s eye condition required urgent medical intervention.

stories.title: Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites
summary: A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed on Sunday shortly after liftoff from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites from Amazon’s Leo internet network in the launch company’s first mission failure.

Both missions successfully delivered their payloads to orbit, but the Pentagon had not yet approved the rocket to resume flying national security payloads, pending its performance with the Amazon mission on Sunday.
The rocket failures have persistently held up Amazon’s bid to rival SpaceX’s vast Starlink internet network, which has more than 11,000 satellites and millions of customers worldwide.

stories.title: Why has the drive to verify India's billion voters put the poll body under scrutiny?
summary: India’s drive to verify the eligibility of roughly a billion voters has put the country’s election authority under severe public scrutiny, with opposition parties alleging the manipulation of voter rolls and exclusion of millions.
Verifying a billion voters: the controversy India started verification of its voter rolls last year ahead of elections in the eastern state of Bihar.
ECI data showed that about 6.5 million voters were excluded from the draft rolls during Bihar’s revision exercise last year.

stories.title: Jay Shah re-elected unopposed as ICC chairman for second term
summary: Jay Shah was re-elected unopposed as chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) for a second two-year term on Monday, extending his leadership of the governing body as cricket prepares for its return to the Olympic Games at Los Angeles in 2028.
Shah’s second term will cover an important period for international cricket, with the sport preparing for its Olympic return after more than a century.
Shah’s second term will run through a period in which the ICC will have to balance the demands of its member boards with the commercial growth of the game and its expanding international programme.

stories.title: India, England, Australia and New Zealand to host all ICC events from 2028-31
summary: The tournament will comprise two groups of five, followed by semi-finals and a final, with the top four teams qualifying for the World Cup.
The winners will progress directly to the 2027 Men’s World Cup Group Stage, while the three remaining teams will compete in the Super Series to determine the final Group Stage spot.
The top two teams from the Global Qualifier will secure the final places at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2028.

stories.title: KWSC completes maintenance work but water shortage persists in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: Although the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) claimed to have restored water supply across the city after completing its annual maintenance work at the Dhabeji pumping station, many areas were still without water for a third consecutive day on Sunday.
It added all 21 pumps at the Dhabeji pumping station were now operational and water supply across the city had been restored.

According to a KWSC spokesperson, during the annual maintenance work, repairs to water pipelines were carried out at Dhabeji, Pipri, Shahrah-i-Bhutto and the Haleji conduits to improve, stabilise and enhance the efficiency of the water supply system.

stories.title: Public parks, playgrounds in Karachi becoming ‘pay-to-play’
summary: Dawn visited several areas in different districts of the city and found that multiple public parks and grounds were being used for paid sporting activities, with private operators charging people for access to various facilities.

Public access increasingly restricted Residents said the growing use of public spaces for paid sporting activities was making it increasingly difficult for children and young people to participate in sports without having to worry about the cost.

A resident living near Eidgah Ground in Korangi questioned why a public facility had been developed if children from the neighbourhood could not use it freely. “What good is it when our children cannot play inside it?

stories.title: Young cloth trader shot dead in Karachi's Gulshan-i-Iqbal
summary: KARACHI: A young man was shot dead in Gulshan-i-Iqbal on Saturday night, officials said on Sunday.
The friends later heard a gunshot and got out of the car, only to find Zafar lying on the road.
But the suspect managed to escape from the police custody.

stories.title: Qaumi Awami Tehreek chief Palijo warns rulers against dismembering provinces, system reset
summary: LARKANA: Qaumi Awami Tehreek (QAT) President Ayaz Latif Palijo has said he believes that PML-N leaders Nawaz Sharif, Maryam Nawaz and Rana Sanaullah have so far kept themselves at distance from the controversial federal plan to create new provinces.
Crackdown claimed Mr Palijo claimed that more than 50 QAT workers were picked up while they were on their way to the venue of this rally.
He termed the police action “deeply regrettable.” Senior QAT leaders told media personnel late in the evening that all detained party workers had since been let off.

stories.title: Medical teaching institutions to abolish trainee registrar post in KP on Dec 1
summary: PESHAWAR: The medical teaching institutions have started abolition of the post of trainee registrar in line with the decision taken by MTI-Policy Board.

PDA says the decision will render 500 doctors jobless besides affecting patient care There are about 500 TRs in medical teaching institutions, whose services will be terminated, according to Provincial Doctors Association (PDA).

It said that Policy Board had already closed the doors of MTIs on civil servants. “Now abolition of TR posts will further hamper patient care as TRs have worked in all departments of MTIs and should be retained,” it added.

stories.title: Karachi mayor lays foundation stone of Rs60m Clifton road project
summary: KARACHI: City Mayor Barrister Murtaza Wahab laid the foundation stone of a development project aimed at improving and rehabilitating Adam Road in Clifton.
Addressing the ceremony, he said that the improvement and rehabilitation work on Adam Road would be carried out along the stretch from Chaudhry Khaliq-uz-Zaman Road, Clifton, to McNeil Road.
The mayor said that, alongside road construction and improvement, the project also included the rehabilitation of the sewerage system.

stories.title: 143 school buildings declared dangerous to be surveyed in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: The District Education Authority (DEA) Rawalpindi will survey 143 dangerous public and private school buildings next week to assess the repair work required, while reconstruction of damaged rooms in five schools has begun.

Talking to Dawn, DEA Rawalpindi Chief Executive Officer Yaseen Baloch said the district administration had surveyed 5,000 private schools and 1,178 government-run schools and found 143 buildings with dangerous rooms.
He said some rooms in these schools required repairs, but none of the buildings had been declared entirely dangerous.

stories.title: Govt reluctant to include farmers in fuel subsidy: Kisan Board Pakistan
summary: LAHORE: The Kisan Board Pakistan (KBP) regrets that the federal government is using delaying tactics about including the agriculture sector in the fuel subsidy scheme of the prime minister.

In a statement on Sunday, KBP Vice President Amanullah Chattha said the government, during talks with the JI on petroleum levy, had promised to include the farming sector in the PM’s fuel subsidy scheme.

However, he added, no step had so far been taken in this respect to the disappointment of wheat growers who are facing an exorbitant increase in the crop’s cost of production due to skyrocketing tariff of diesel.

stories.title: Separate legislative assembly in Islamabad on the cards
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government has intensified its efforts to set up a separate legislative assembly in Islamabad.

When contacted, a senior government officer said that it was clear that a new, separate legislative assembly would be set up in Islamabad. “As far as making Haripur, Rawalpindi and Murree part of Islamabad is concerned, nothing is final yet.
But yes, Islamabad will have a separate legislative assembly,” he said.

stories.title: Historic Malot Fort in Chakwal presents a picture of neglect
summary: Described as the most beautiful fort in the Salt Range, Malot has been the subject of two consecutive projects undertaken by the Punjab Archaeology Department and the Tourism Development Corporation of Punjab (TDCP) for its conservation, restoration and development.
The temple in Malot village holds a unique position among the temples of the Salt Range because of its imposing gateway, which was probably constructed at a later date.
Another project for the beautification and development of Malot Fort is being undertaken by the TDCP.

stories.title: 23 arrested for holding dog fight in Punjab's Cholistan
summary: BAHAWALPUR: The Saddar Police Yazman arrested 23 suspects for organising a dog fight in a remote village of Cholistan on Sunday.
The district police spokesperson, Muhammad Naeem, said Saddar Yazman police raided the dog fight venue at Toba Goha Warr at Chak 76/DB near Bohranwali Colony.
The police arrested 23 persons involved in gambling on their dogs.

stories.title: China-developed 10-ton e-aircraft completes first piloted flight
summary: SHANGHAI: China’s independently developed 10-ton electric commercial aircraft CE-25A completed its maiden piloted flight on Saturday, according to the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC).
The CE-25A is COMAC’s first electric commercial aircraft.
The aircraft completed its first unmanned autonomous flight on Feb 2 this year.

stories.title: Jamaat-i-Islami wants new units through Constitution, people’s will
summary: LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman has said the JI is not opposed to the creation of new administrative units but the process must strictly follow constitutional procedures and reflect the will of the people.
On the petroleum levy issue, Mr Rehman said the JI had handed over its final draft to the government, proposing a reduction in petroleum prices and a gradual withdrawal of the levy.
Announcing preparations for the gathering at Minar-i-Pakistan, Mr Rehman said a comprehensive public mobilisation campaign would precede the event.

stories.title: World Bank ‘satisfied’ with $370m National Health Support Programme
summary: Effective since October 2022, the NHSP aims to advance universal health coverage by strengthening equitable access to and the quality of essential healthcare services at the primary level.

Govt claims goods exports reached ‘all-time high’ of $11.4bn in July-October “Provincial governments have shown strong ownership, and the reforms introduced through the Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs) are strengthening primary health care systems.
According to the World Bank, the programme’s improved health facility readiness score has reached 75pc in KP, 80pc in Punjab and 77.5pc in Sindh.

stories.title: PSX rallies over 3,000 points on broad-based buying
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) opened the new trading week on a strong note on Monday, with investors stepping up buying across major sectors, driving the benchmark index up by more than 3,000 points in early afternoon trading despite a subdued trend across Asian markets.
The buying momentum remained strong through most of the session, although the market experienced some intermittent fluctuations.
After gaining 1,809.88 points at 9:39am, the index extended its advance and reached 258,146.77, up 3,104.31 points, or 1.

summary: Bushra Bibi told the lawyers that doctors had advised another critical surgical procedure and warned that an infection following the operation could lead to “complete and permanent loss of vision”, according to the application.
The petition said the jail authorities had not provided Bushra Bibi, her family or her legal team with medical notes, diagnostic reports or prescriptions.

stories.title: Punjab working on first AI-run climate observatory
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Climate Observatory will be a milestone in the province’s efforts to address climate change, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said on Sunday.
The facility would also house environmental data resources and research laboratories, providing young climate scientists with opportunities for learning and research, she added.
The chief minister hoped the project would bring international scientific cooperation and research partnerships under one roof, while supporting evidence-based policymaking and public awareness.

stories.title: Water demand outstrips supply in Punjab: UN agency
summary: The gap between water supply and demand has become particularly acute in Punjab’s urban areas because of limited access to freshwater and declining groundwater reserves, the report observed.
The analysis estimated that Punjab needed an additional 10 billion cubic metres of usable water annually to bridge the supply-demand gap and sustain its groundwater aquifer.
The report also observed that groundwater recharge sources had diminished, reducing the province’s net renewable water resources.

stories.title: Yemeni army says troops regrouping to break Houthi siege of Taiz
summary: Yemen’s army said on Sunday that it was repositioning troops to help break the Houthi siege of Taiz, while the group claimed that government forces had been driven from positions near the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
The statement followed an announcement by government-aligned forces that they were pulling back from Bab al-Mandeb and neighbouring Dhubab on the Red Sea coast.
Government forces announced the recapture of the Bab al-Mandeb area and parts of Dhubab in early October, about a month after the Houthis seized the area.

stories.title: Punjab sugar millers snub order to begin crushing from weekend
summary: Khalid Hussain Bath, president of a farmers’ group, said the government’s notification proved ineffective, with mills remaining closed in Punjab and crushing yet to begin in Sindh.
Bath demanded that the government immediately announce a sugarcane support price, ensure mills purchase all approved crop varieties and provide surplus sugar to farmers.
According to official sources, mills will determine sugarcane prices under a market-based mechanism while the provincial government monitors rates to safeguard growers’ interests.

stories.title: President terms hate speech in digital space deadly threat
summary: In his message on the occasion of International Day for Tolerance being observed on Monday, President Zardari highlighted the need for all Pakistanis to help build a society where every person can live with dignity.

The International Day for Tolerance is observed annually on Nov 16 to raise awareness about dangers of intolerance and promote mutual understanding, respect, and peace among diverse cultures and communities.

Recalling that our non-Muslim citizens have helped build this country, the president asserted that every worshipper must feel protected in his place of worship. “Tolerance also requires us to respect differences of language, culture, belief and political opinion.

stories.title: CDA finalises revised PC-I for Islamabad cricket stadium at Rs16.7bn
summary: According to the CDA, the stadium will have a seating capacity of 35,000, making it the largest cricket stadium in Pakistan.
However, the CDA maintains that sports and recreational activities are permissible in the zone and that the construction of a cricket stadium falls within the permitted activities.
This time, the CDA itself is undertaking the construction of the cricket stadium.

stories.title: Use of technology must be in harmony with fair trial provision: PHC
summary: While allowing the virtual appearance of the complainant/witness, the bench issued multiple directives to the trial court under the said rules so as to ensure fair trial.

The bench ordered that if the requisite safeguards couldn’t effectively be secured through video conferencing, the trial court should consider requiring the physical appearance of the witness or adopting any other mode permissible under CrPC and Qanun-i-Shahadat Order.

The bench directed the trial court to ascertain that an authorised virtual assistant, nominated by the Peshawar district and sessions judge was present at the virtual court point, and that the identity of the witness should be verified in accordance with Rule 8(5) to (7).

stories.title: Mansehra residents resent gas supply suspension
summary: Meanwhile, gas supply to compressed natural gas (CNG) stations across the city and its suburbs was also suspended several times over the last two days. “We do not know why the supplies are being suspended.
We approached SNGPL officials, but they did not tell us the exact reason,” the operator of a CNG station said.

stories.title: Mohmand elders oppose land acquisition plan for police lines, jail
summary: The elders held a jirga with members of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) to express their reservations over the proposed land acquisition.

During the meeting, local elders, including Haji Saman, Maulana Sardar, Malik Mukammal Shah, Haji Mukarram, Haji Faraz, Haji Misal and Haji Zaitullah, maintained that the disputed land was their ancestral property and residential area.
According to the administration, Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act has been invoked to acquire the land for the proposed construction of police lines, a jail and a district judicial complex.
